meta.title: Ten changes for a steadier booking service
meta.lede: Six small changes and four large ones for the booking service, found by reading its code. One choice first: a faster checkout or safer changes. Pick by number.

options.label: A faster checkout
options.summary: Cut the round trips and slow calls riders wait through at the Friday peak.

options.label: Safer changes
options.summary: Tests, flags, and clear errors, so a change stops breaking checkout.

parts.markdown:
The booking service is a Go service over Postgres that the rider app and the harbour office both call. Four people build it, with agents writing most of the code.

These ideas come from reading all of it: 212 files, about 31,000 lines of Go and SQL, and the last 90 days of traces and incidents. Most of the pain sits on one path, from search to a paid booking, and most incidents began with a change to that path.

Effort is agent time, not calendar time.

parts.title: The path from search to a paid booking. Holds live inside one process, and payments retry without a key.
parts.source:
flowchart LR
  app[Rider app] --> api[Gateway]
  api --> search[Search]
  api --> checkout[Checkout]:::accent
  search --> fares[Fares]:::violet
  checkout --> fares
  checkout --> holds[Seat holds]:::risk
  checkout --> pay[Payments]:::risk
  fares --> db[(Postgres)]
  holds -.-> mem[(In-process map)]:::risk
  pay -->|retries, no key| card[Card provider]

parts.markdown: At the Friday evening peak, a booking takes 3.2 seconds from tapping Book to the confirmation, and one attempt in forty times out. Payments and fares account for most of the wait.

parts.title: A retry can charge twice
parts.markdown: When the card provider is slow, checkout retries the charge without an idempotency key. Twice in 90 days a rider paid twice for one booking. Idea 2 closes this whichever way the cycle goes.

items.title: Quote every leg in one query
items.summary: Fares for a whole trip load in one query instead of one per leg, which removes most of the wait in the fares step.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown:
`FareFor` becomes `FaresFor` in `fares/store.go`, and `Quote` reads from the map it returns:

```postgresql
SELECT route_id, class, price FROM fares
WHERE (route_id, class) IN (SELECT * FROM unnest($1::text[], $2::text[]))
```

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Fares is the second slowest step, and almost all of it is round trips. A return trip for a family of four makes eight queries today.

facets.label: In use
facets.markdown: The trace for a return booking shows one fares query, and the step drops to about 90 ms.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Idea 7 caches the same map.

items.title: An idempotency key on every charge
items.summary: Each checkout sends one key with its charge and every retry, so a slow card provider can never charge a rider twice.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Checkout makes one key for each payment, stores it on the booking row, and `payments/charge.go` sends it as `Idempotency-Key` on the first call and on every retry.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Two riders were charged twice in 90 days, both after a provider timeout, and each refund took the harbour office 25 minutes.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Idea 9 reuses the key to refund exactly once.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: A key kept only in memory is lost on a restart mid-checkout, which is why it lives on the booking row.

items.title: Typed errors from the payments client
items.summary: The payments client returns declined, retryable, and fatal errors as values the caller can test, not messages it has to match.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: `payments/client.go` wraps provider codes in `ErrDeclined`, `ErrRetryable`, and `ErrFatal`. Checkout switches on `errors.Is` instead of `strings.Contains(err.Error(), "timeout")`.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Three incidents started when the provider reworded an error message. With types, the compiler and the tests catch that instead of riders.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: Ideas 2 and 9 retry only `ErrRetryable`.

items.title: One request id in every log line
items.summary: A request id from the gateway reaches every log line and outgoing call, so one checkout reads as one story.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Middleware in `api/middleware.go` puts the id in the context, `internal/log` adds it to every line, and the fares and payments clients forward it as `X-Request-Id`.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Following a failed checkout today means matching timestamps across four logs. It took two hours in the last incident.

facets.label: In use
facets.markdown: Searching the logs for one id shows the whole booking, from search to the card provider's answer.

items.title: Contract tests for the fares API
items.summary: Recorded app requests pin what the rider app expects from the fares endpoint, so CI fails before a change breaks the app.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: `fares/contract_test.go` replays the app's recorded requests from `testdata/app-fares/` against the handler and compares every response field by name and type.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Two releases broke the app by renaming a fares field, and both passed every test the service had.

facets.label: Note
facets.markdown: The app team records new requests with one command when the app changes.

items.title: Free seat holds when checkout gives up
items.summary: A failed or abandoned checkout frees its held spaces at once instead of waiting fifteen minutes for them to expire.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Checkout's error path and the app's back button call `holds.Release`. Expiry stays as the backstop for a rider who closes the app.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: At the peak, abandoned holds keep up to 30 car spaces off sale, and riders see a sailing as full when it is not.

items.title: Cache quotes for thirty seconds
items.summary: Search, the trip screen, and checkout share one short-lived quote, so a rider's fare is worked out once per trip.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: `fares/cache.go` keys quotes by route, date, class, and party, keeps them for 30 seconds, and drops them all when fares change by bumping a version.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: A rider sees the same quote on three screens, and each screen asks for it again. At the peak that is a third of all fares queries.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: A stale price must never reach payment. Checkout checks the fares version again before it charges and requotes if it moved.

items.title: Seat holds in a lease table
items.summary: Holds move from a map inside one process to a Postgres table, so deploys keep them and two instances can take bookings.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: A `hold_leases` table with a unique index on sailing and space. Holds are taken with `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` and swept when they expire, and `holds/holds.go` keeps its interface.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Holds live in memory today, so the service cannot run a second instance, and every deploy drops the holds of riders mid-checkout.

facets.label: In use
facets.markdown: A deploy at the Friday peak goes unnoticed, and the gateway spreads checkouts across two instances.

facets.label: Unlocks
facets.markdown: A second instance at the Friday peak, which halves the queue in front of every checkout step.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: A mistake here double books car spaces. Run both stores side by side for a week and compare every hold before switching.

items.title: Refunds on a queue with retries
items.summary: Refunds leave the request path for a worker that retries with backoff and records every attempt.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: Cancelling a booking writes a `refund_jobs` row. A worker in `refunds/worker.go` sends it with the charge's key and retries `ErrRetryable` with backoff.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: A slow refund holds the cancel screen for up to 20 seconds today, and a failed one is lost unless the rider calls.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: A stuck queue delays refunds without a sound. Alert when the oldest job is more than ten minutes old.

items.title: Ship checkout changes behind flags
items.summary: A checkout change can go out switched off, reach a share of riders, and be turned off again without a rollback.

facets.label: How it works
facets.markdown: A small flag store in `internal/flags`, read from Postgres every 30 seconds and checked in `checkout/handler.go`, plus a `flags` command for the team.

facets.label: Why
facets.markdown: Seven of the last eleven incidents began with a checkout change, and each one took a full rollback to undo.

facets.label: In use
facets.markdown: A new payment screen reaches 5% of riders on Monday, half on Wednesday, and everyone once its error rate holds.

facets.label: Risk
facets.markdown: Old flags pile up. Each flag gets an owner and a removal date when it is added.

items.title: Rewrite checkout in Rust
items.summary: The time goes to round trips and the card provider, not to Go, so a rewrite would move none of it.

items.title: Split booking into microservices
items.summary: Four people run this, and more services would add the very network hops that slow checkout.

items.title: A GraphQL gateway for the apps
items.summary: The app's calls are few and cheap, and idea 7 removes the repeated ones.
